new_targets.why: Coinbase AgentKit is the reference toolkit for AI agents with crypto wallet and payment capabilities. Backed by Coinbase, widely referenced across the x402 and agent-payment ecosystem. A merged PR here would be the highest-credibility proof point in the portfolio — it signals Coinbase's team thought the integration was worth shipping.
new_targets.gap: AgentKit manages wallet keys, network selection, and payment primitives for autonomous agents — but any process with the right env vars can invoke it with full spend permissions. There is no credential layer that scopes which agent instance is authorized to spend, at what limit, or for which payee. Bolyra's FINANCIAL_SMALL/MEDIUM/UNLIMITED bits map directly onto AgentKit's action surface.
new_targets.suggested_pr: docs/example: add Bolyra agent credential check before AgentKit payment or transaction action
new_targets.contact_hint: Coinbase OSS team is professional and responsive. Check CONTRIBUTING.md and CLA requirements first. Target the docs/ or examples/ directory — a standalone example file is safest.

new_targets.why: OpenAI's official Python SDK for building multi-agent systems. Extremely high visibility — every developer building OpenAI-based agents sees this repo. A Bolyra integration example here reaches the largest possible audience in the target ecosystem, without requiring anything from OpenAI (it's an external example).
new_targets.gap: The SDK orchestrates hand-offs between agents and tool calls with no concept of which agent instance holds what authorization scope. An operator running 10 agents cannot enforce that only 3 of them are allowed to call financial tools, or that a delegated sub-agent cannot exceed the delegator's permissions. Bolyra adds credential-gated tool invocation without modifying the orchestration layer.
new_targets.suggested_pr: docs/example: add Bolyra credential gate for scoped tool authorization in multi-agent pipelines
new_targets.contact_hint: OpenAI reviews external contributions carefully. Target examples/ or cookbook-style directory. Keep PR minimal — one Python file, no new deps, zero modifications to core SDK.

new_targets.why: AutoGen is Microsoft's multi-agent framework — one of the most-starred agent repos on GitHub. Enterprise-heavy audience (the ICP for Bolyra's B2B play). A Bolyra integration in AutoGen hits the exact buyer persona: enterprise developers who need audit trails and authorization controls for autonomous agent actions.
new_targets.gap: AutoGen orchestrates complex agent conversations and tool use with no authorization layer. An agent in a group chat can call any registered tool without the orchestrator verifying it holds the right credentials. Bolyra adds per-agent credential checks before tool execution — critical for enterprise deployments where compliance matters.
new_targets.suggested_pr: docs/example: add Bolyra per-agent authorization before AutoGen tool calls
new_targets.contact_hint: Large repo with active maintainers. Check CONTRIBUTING.md — Microsoft repos typically require a CLA. Target the notebook examples or docs/examples directory.

new_targets.why: Pydantic AI is a fast-growing Python agent framework from the Pydantic team (trusted Python ecosystem authors). Strong traction in the Python developer community. No auth/identity layer — structured outputs and tool calling are the focus, not authorization.
new_targets.gap: Pydantic AI agents call tools and interact with external APIs with no credential check on the agent context. Any agent with the right configuration can call any registered tool. Bolyra adds: before a tool is invoked, verify the calling agent holds an AgentPolicy credential with the appropriate permission bit. Works as a tool wrapper with no framework modification.
new_targets.suggested_pr: docs/example: add Bolyra credential gate as a Pydantic AI tool wrapper for authorization
new_targets.contact_hint: Pydantic team is professional and technically rigorous. Example must be clean and idiomatic. Check CLA requirements.

new_targets.why: LangGraph (from LangChain team) is the leading graph-based multi-agent orchestration framework — distinct codebase from crewAI (PR #5 in portfolio). High-traffic repo with active maintainers. LangGraph's stateful graph model makes per-node authorization a natural fit: each node in the graph can check the agent credential before executing.
new_targets.gap: LangGraph nodes execute arbitrary tool calls and LLM invocations with no authorization layer. A graph can be set up to call financial APIs without any check that the agent running the graph has been granted financial permissions. Bolyra integrates cleanly as a node-level guard: before the node executes, verify the active agent credential covers the action.
new_targets.suggested_pr: docs/example: add Bolyra authorization node as a guard in LangGraph agent workflows
new_targets.contact_hint: LangChain team is very PR-active — they ship docs and examples fast. Target the examples/ or how-tos/ directory. Mention the existing crewAI integration (PR #5) as credibility.
